correctness.rationale: For A=U diag(sqrt(a_i)) with right singular vectors coordinate-aligned, a_i>0, d≥3, q≥0, one iid nonzero centered unit-variance real probe, the one-column projection residual is ∑a_i−∑a_i b_iW_i/∑b_iW_i, b_i=a_i^(2q+1). Swap-symmetrization of exchangeable positive W_i shows α_j−α_i=(b_i−b_j)E[(W_i−W_j)^2/(2SS_swap)], giving the claimed sum of nonnegative pair terms and strict equality cases. Finiteness requires only E W_i=1 and S>0, not 4th moments. In spike family H=L^(2q+1), sign excess=(L−1)(d−1)/(H+d−1), Gaussian excess=(L−1)E[(1−T)/(1+(H−1)T)] with T~Beta(1/2,(d−1)/2). Dominated convergence under u=Ht yields sharp H^(−1/2) constant. Independently enumerated 18 positive finite-law products with exact fractions and checked pairwise identity.

Their minimax result cannot imply this fixed-orientation expected residual identity.

value.rationale: A genuine design rule for the simplest randomized subspace-iteration building block: constant-magnitude sign probes minimize expected squared error for fixed aligned spectra, with quantified excess of all competing iid magnitudes and a sharp Gaussian power-iteration decay penalty. The alignment and one-column restrictions are explicit mathematical boundaries.

limitations: Only coordinate-aligned right singular directions and one sketch column

Expected squared Frobenius rather than spectral norm or arbitrary orientation
Spike asymptotic q→∞ with L,d fixed
